chunks: Ibn Mahboub, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Returning an answer to a letter is obligatory, like the obligation of returning the greeting, and the one who initiates the greeting is closer to Allah and His Messenger.

key_terms.الْبَادِي بِالسَّلَامِ: The one who initiates the greeting
key_terms.رَدُّ جَوَابِ الْكِتَابِ: Returning an answer to a letter

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on replying to a letter and the merit of initiating greetings?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes the replying to a letter as a mandatory duty (wajib), drawing a direct legal parallel to the obligation of returning a greeting, thereby elevating written correspondence to the status of social and spiritual etiquette. The hadith further emphasizes the virtue of the initiator, suggesting that the one who begins the exchange holds a closer spiritual station to Allah and the Prophet, reflecting the broader Islamic emphasis on initiating goodwill (bid' al-salam).

en.hubeali:
Ibn Mahboub, from Abdullah Bin Sinan, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Returning an answer to a letter is as Obligatory as the Obligation of returning the greeting, and the initiator of the greeting is closer with Allah<sup>azwj</sup> and His<sup>azwj</sup> Rasool<sup>saww</sup>’.
en.sarwar: 2. Ibn Mahbub has narrated from ‘Abd Allah ibn Sinan from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following: “
It is necessary to reply a letter just as it is necessary to answer a greeting of peace. The initiator of a greeting of peace is closer to Allah and His messenger.”
